clue.text: Official has opportunity to make a U-turn

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance

indicators.note: the U of U-turn says the turn faces back the other way, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: a roll is a turn, as an aircraft rolls over

explanation.surface: A government official seizes the moment to reverse a policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated word splits in two: 'U-' is the reversal signal and 'turn' the word it acts on. The surface's political climbdown is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancellor is a senior state or university officer, so an official.

clue.text: Food caught when out on the river

definitions.text: caught when out on the river
definitions.meaning: a rower who mistimes a stroke and has the oar jammed in the water is said to catch one

explanation.surface: A meal hooked while out boating.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab is a shellfish eaten as seafood, and 'catching a crab' is a rowing blunder where the oar snags.

clue.text: Car not moving is a car still?

definitions.text: Car not moving is a car still?

parts.words: Car not moving is a car still?
parts.note: take the mobile out of the long word for a car and what is left still names a car

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether a parked car is still a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is short for automobile, so it remains a word for a car.

clue.text: Stubborn Scotsman first to count out debtors' notes

indicators.note: first says the scrambled count leads, ahead of the Scotsman
out means the letters of the word count are knocked out of order

parts.note: Mac, from the common surname prefix, is crossword shorthand for a Scotsman
an IOU is a note of debt, so debtors' notes are IOUS

explanation.surface: An obstinate Scot is first in line to tally up the IOUs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles COUNT into CONTU, and 'first' puts that ahead of MAC; IOUS ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumacious means wilfully disobedient to authority, i.e. obstinate.

clue.text: Pound a point minimum

parts.note: L is short for pound sterling, from Latin libra
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone asks for at least a pound and a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound comes from the Latin libra, as in the £ sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means the smallest amount, i.e. the lowest possible.

clue.text: Happening to come about payment

parts.note: to come about is to occur
rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: A rent payment happens to fall due.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurrent means taking place now, i.e. going on.

clue.text: Transfer licence

definitions.meaning: to hand something on, as a footballer moves the ball to a teammate
a permit allowing entry or travel

explanation.surface: A football club official arranges a player's move and his permit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is to hand over to another, and a pass is a permit granting admission.

clue.text: Get moving by firm footwork

parts.note: a driver presses a pedal down hard with the foot to pick up speed

explanation.surface: Advice to a dancer to step out briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: To accelerate is to speed up, done in a car by pushing the pedal.

clue.text: Sent out and crying perhaps such strictness!

indicators.note: out says the letters of the two words are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone sent out of the room in tears complains of harsh discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of SENT and CRYING together; 'perhaps' just softens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringency is severity or rigour in rules.

clue.text: Gate shows hour at which the ball finishes

indicators.note: the ball finishes things off, so its word comes at the end of the run

parts.note: taken as written
ten is an hour of the clock
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A notice tells guests the time when the ball ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gate' is not a door: in sport it is the number of spectators at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports gate is the crowd count or takings, i.e. how many turned up.

clue.text: Cliff gets a mark

definitions.meaning: a steep rocky outcrop on a hillside, a northern English word
a lasting blemish left by a healed wound

explanation.surface: A climber's fall from a crag leaves a lasting blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is both a rocky crag in northern English hills and the trace of an old wound.

clue.text: If in doubt put it in writing?

definitions.text: If in doubt put it in writing?

parts.words: If in doubt put it in writing?
parts.note: a writer unsure of something adds the punctuation for a query

explanation.surface: Advice to get things on paper when unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: The query sign ends a written question, expressing uncertainty.

clue.text: Material for, say, gaggin' a goat?

parts.note: a goat butts with its head, so it is a butter

indicators.note: say marks a word spoken, giving a fabric's name that matches muzzlin' when spoken

parts.note: gagging a mouth is muzzling it, dropped g and all

explanation.surface: A whimsical query about what cloth would shut a goat up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but signals a homophone; the goat is a BUTTER because it butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter muslin is a loosely woven cotton cloth, used for straining and wrapping dairy produce.

clue.text: Student in favour sets down names of trouble-makers

indicators.note: in says the student's letter goes inside the word for favour

parts.note: to back someone is to favour them
L is the learner sign on a student driver's car
to list is to set down in order

explanation.surface: A student in favour writes down the names of troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the British learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Blacklists are rolls of people to be shunned or barred.

clue.text: After a round girl is above the limit — having to have far too much

indicators.note: after says the girl follows the round shape
is above places the girl over the limit in this down entry

parts.note: O is round in shape
Vera is a girl's name
a bound is a limit

explanation.surface: After a drink, a girl is over the limit and has had far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is above' only works because this is a down answer, where one piece sits on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To overabound is to be present in excess, i.e. to be overly plentiful.

clue.text: Adore Granny Smith fruit

parts.note: to adore is to love
a Granny Smith is a green variety of apple

explanation.surface: Someone declares devotion to a favourite green apple.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit is not an apple at all: 'love apple' is an old name for the tomato.
explanation.definitionFit: Love apple is an archaic name for the tomato, botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Poet pines in a way for earthy material

indicators.note: in a way says the letters of poet pines are arranged in another manner

explanation.surface: A poet yearns, in his fashion, for clay.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of POET PINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipestone is a soft reddish clay stone carved by Native Americans into tobacco pipes.

clue.text: Wait for opening of play

definitions.meaning: to wait at table, attending to diners
in tennis, each point starts with a player hitting the ball over the net

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hold on until a show's premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve is to wait on diners, and a serve is the stroke that starts each tennis point.

clue.text: Is Gee whiz! A soldier and his dog

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gee whiz
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a soldier with his pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a Cockney exclamation of surprise; GI is the standard US soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: Garibaldi responsible for flag-waving

parts.note: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the Italian nationalist hero of unification
IC stands for in charge, i.e. responsible

explanation.surface: The Italian hero is blamed for nationalist fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: A Garibaldi is also a British currant biscuit, but here it is the man, Italy's great nationalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag-waving describes loud love of one's country, i.e. nationalistic.

clue.text: Party economy introduced to make things easier

parts.note: Labour is a major British political party
economy means thrift, a saving

explanation.surface: A political party brings in thrift measures to ease life.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Labour Party gives the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour-saving gadgets reduce effort, easing tasks.

clue.text: Getting round a king to act against drink

indicators.note: getting round turns the whole string back to front

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
to act is to do
v, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A king tries to fight off his drinking habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting round' reverses the whole run A, K, DO, V into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear spirit, a strong alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Society has a mace

definitions.meaning: a heavy weapon with a spiked head

explanation.surface: A society owns a ceremonial staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a members' association and also a heavy stick or cudgel, like a mace.

clue.text: Rescue charge is about right

indicators.note: is about says the charge surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A rescue fee is about right.
explanation.definitionFit: To free is to release, as in liberating a captive.

clue.text: Herein lies trouble for the starter

definitions.text: Herein lies trouble for the starter

parts.words: Herein lies trouble for the starter
parts.note: to be 'in' this dish is to be in trouble, and it is also served as a first course

explanation.surface: A warning that the opening course is where problems lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is a typical first course, and 'in the soup' is an idiom for being in trouble.

clue.text: Apparatus reminiscent of Stentor

parts.note: Stentor was the Greek herald in the Iliad whose voice was as loud as fifty men's, so the device recalls him by amplifying speech

explanation.surface: A device that recalls a famously loud-voiced figure of Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudhailer is a hand-held megaphone that amplifies the voice, like a stentorian herald.

clue.text: Party pride

definitions.meaning: one team or faction in a contest or dispute
airs and swagger, as in putting on airs

explanation.surface: A political faction's self-regard.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team or faction, and 'side' is also old slang for haughty pretension.

clue.text: Observation clever and worth noting

parts.note: an observation is a remark
able means clever or skilled

explanation.surface: A shrewd comment deserves attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable means notable, deserving attention.
